$comment: GH-799 (queue item "Zones", stage C0) - THE ZONE TYPES, ONE FILE, ONE READER.
WHAT IS NOT HERE ANY MORE. This file first carried a second vocabulary beside the zone types: the
four kinds of water source (`bore`, `surface`, `recycled`, `potable`), for a column of `samples`
that this stage was going to add. The owner's decision of 01.10.2026, taken after she was shown
all three readers of the word that carries that meaning today -- the sample list, the trend on the
screen and the water sparklines in the document, none of which changes a number on the stand --
is that a water sample keeps ONLY ITS NAME. So the column is not added and the vocabulary is not
declared: a list of allowed values with nothing that may hold one is a promise with no writer.
`payload._zone` on a water sample is untouched, and what becomes of it is a separate plan.
WHY A FILE AND NOT A TABLE. The analyst's decision of 01.10.2026, and its reason: these values
are owned by the CODE, not by a person. Nobody enters them in the interface, there is no screen
that edits the dictionary, and a table would have added two tables and two seeds to the migration
while answering the same question. The same shape as `aa-ranges.json` and the inputs list: the
server reads this file, pages get it parsed from the server, and there is no copy in `assets` --
`Gh799TheZoneTypesHaveOneFileTest` reddens if a second reader appears.
A zone keeps its type as a KEY of this file (`zones.zone_type`, NULL allowed). That is what the
owner's decision of 22.09.2026 asks for -- a reference to a declared value rather than free text
-- so a key this file does not carry is refused by the server.
NULL IS THE EXPECTED STATE AFTER THE TRANSFER, and it is the owner's decision of 22.09.2026:
"you can leave it empty, and I will fill them in by hand afterwards". A guessed type with a mark
beside it looks like a filled field and may never be returned to; an empty one asks to be filled.
No figure depends on it: the type is not an input of any calculation.
WHERE THE VALUES AND THE WORDS COME FROM, so that no number here is invented: the keys and the
labels are moved as they stand from `sample-switcher-ui.js` (`ZONE_LABELS`, the switcher's own
table, whose own rows for the water sources stay where they are) and `prebbles-products.js`'s
cotula key; `areaGuidance` is moved from `AREA_GUIDANCE` in
`sample-manager.js`, hectares and sentences unchanged. Those tables stay where they are until
stage C4 moves their readers; this file does not race them, and the equality is held by the test
named above.
`cotula_bowling_green` has no entry in either live table -- it is a surface type elsewhere in the
product (`prebbles-products.js`, `nutrition-program-inputs.js`) and the plan declares it as the
twelfth zone type. Its label is the name the product already prints for it; its area guidance is
the permissive `other` row rather than a number nobody measured, and that is said here rather
than left to be discovered.
GH-804 (part 1) - `zoneTypeField` IS NOT HERE ANY MORE, and this is where it went: the obligation
on a zone's type is declared in `calculation-inputs.schema.json` as the input `zones.zoneType`,
read through `CalculationInputs`. An obligation declared in two files is two obligations, and the
inputs list is the place this product declares what a calculation needs. This file keeps what it
was always for: the twelve types themselves. The paragraphs below are the reasons the block was
written, kept because they are the reasons it reads as it does -- they now describe the entry in
the other file.
GH-801 (stage C2) - `zoneTypeField`: THE OBLIGATION WAS DECLARED HERE, NOT WRITTEN INTO A SCREEN.
The owner's decision of 01.10.2026 is that a zone's type is required, and her answer to HOW is the
variant (b) she was shown with its price: the Zones tab saves nothing while the site still has a
zone with no type. `judgedOn: result` is that answer in one word -- the save is judged by the set
of zones the site is LEFT with, not by the rows the request happens to mention, so the way out is
always open: choose the types (and delete what is spare) in one save and it is accepted.
WHY NOT IN `calculation-inputs.schema.json`, where every other obligation of this product lives:
that list holds the INPUTS OF A SITE, one value each, read by the calculation and by the panel that
names what could not be computed. A zone type is neither -- a site has from none to many zones, a
site with no zones owes nothing, and no figure anywhere depends on the type (measured, plan section
1.1). Putting it there would have made the wizard ask for it and the run record report it missing.
`requiredIn` AND `notRequiredIn` ARE BOTH DECLARED, because where the obligation does NOT hold is
the owner's decision too, in her words: "we do not change the add interface". A zone arriving from
the Data page or from an import is created with no type and nothing is refused; the type is asked
for in the one place she named. A reader that judged by storage alone could not tell those apart.
`place` IS THE WORDS A PERSON READS, spelled as the screen spells them, the same shape as the
`places` map of the inputs list.

$comment: GH-806 (queue item "Zones", stage SZh1) - THE WORDS THE SPRAY JOURNAL STORES, AND WHICH TYPE EACH IS.
WHY A TABLE AND NOT A GUESS. The journal has never held a zone of a site: it holds a WORD per entry,
chosen from a list of its own (`spray-log-ui.js` offers greens/tees/fairways/surrounds/sportsground/
other; the Data page's own form offers Greens/Tees/Fairways/Surrounds/Roughs/Other). The owner's
decision of 01.10.2026 is that an entry carries the TYPE OF A ZONE by its identifier, so each of
those words needs an answer, and the answer is declared here beside the types rather than worked out
by whoever happens to read it.
`noType` IS AN ANSWER TOO, and the more important half. `surrounds` and `sportsground` are words the
journal offers for which this dictionary declares no type: the nearest keys would be a guess
(`approach`? `collar`? `sports_pitch`?), and a guessed type is the substitution this whole queue item
removes. They are listed so that a word with no type is told apart from a word nobody declared - the
first is left without a type, the second stops the transfer.
GH-816: a word added to `noType` must not be one that can mean a green. `analysisZoneTypes` counts a
golf course's application only by the type `green`, so an entry written with such a word would stop
counting for the analysis without anything saying so.
MEASURED, 02.10.2026: of the five entries the journal holds, four carry `greens` and one carries
`other`; `surrounds`, `sportsground` and `roughs` appear in no stored row at all. `all` is NOT a
stored word and is not declared here - it is a cache key inside `spray-log.js` (`opts.zone || 'all'`),
which is a correction to the plan's own dry-run line.
COMPARED WITHOUT CASE, because the server stores the word as it was sent (`normaliseZones` trims and
nothing else) and the two lists above are spelled differently.
GH-816 (queue item "Zones", ZhT) - WHICH APPLICATIONS OF THE SPRAY JOURNAL THE ANALYSIS COUNTS, BY THE SITE'S TURF TYPE.
The owner's decision of 02.10.2026, variant (b): on a sports site and a lawn an application to a zone
of ANY type counts; on a golf course only an application to a green does. The keys are the turf types
of calculation-inputs.schema.json; a value is a list of zone types of this file, or the declared word
for any type. The server reads it through ZoneTypes::analysisZoneTypesFor, for the spray-log context
the calculation asks and for the run start's "PGR filled in" -- one rule, two readers.
